scope: Proposition 8.1 (The decorated lattice) of the manuscript “A negative solution to the finite lattice representation problem” (preprints/A-Negative-Solution-to-the-Finite-Lattice-Representation-Problem-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a102efd4a3009423), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 67-68. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: There is a finite nonempty lattice L with the following properties. The properties hold in either orientation of L, using the corresponding Boolean and detector components. (i) The lattice contains a bounded copy of the original B4. Every proper nonzero original Boolean vertex v has both [0, v] and [v, 1] fenced. The global interval [0, 1] is fenced. (ii) There are original detector vertices d1, d2, X, z with 0 < di < X < z < 1. The intervals [0, di], [0, X], [X, 1] and [z, 1] are fenced. Every coatom of [0, X] is above a di. (iii) In any finite subgroup-interval representation L ∼ = [D, G], the simple labels of every proper nonzero original Boolean vertex, of d1, d2, and of X equal the simple label of G. 67 (iv) Let 0 < v < u < 1 be comparable original Boolean vertices. In any finite subgroup-interval representation [v, 1]op ∼ = [A, Uv], the labels of the vertices corresponding to u and v, taken relative to the common bottom A, are defined and equal. The same assertion holds for the detector pair (z, X) in any representation [X, 1]op ∼ = [A, UX]. In (iv), no representation of the entire dual lattice is assumed. If several such upper filters have compatible realizations with a common bottom A, the conclusions hold in that compatible system.
